svg.title: A pile of water-worn, bleached driftwood on a river gravel bar: seven barkless logs of different lengths, thicknesses and angles lying loosely across one another in a low, random, lopsided pile - six together and one lying apart on the beach in front - none parallel, none stood up or leaned, none steeper than twenty degrees, none woven over-and-under. ATTEMPT SEVEN, 2026-09-24, AND WHAT IT CORRECTS: blind run bde36c08332f59f9 read attempt six as A BEAVER DAM, and attempt six's torn ends tapered into spikes, which read as gnawed or whittled points. So every end here is WATER-WORN: blunt, as wide as the log right to the end, rounded over by the water into an irregular, lopsided bevel with one shallow worn dip - never a point, never a flat sawn face, and never a knob or ball wider than the shaft. The wood is silver-grey first: six logs take all three tones of the `path` ramp and one takes `limestone`, the light tone on the upper body with a wandering lower edge, the base tone below it, and the shade tone as a thin rim along the underside and in two to four grain checks per log; each log carries one split opening from a worn end, three carry a short worn limb stub, and the thickest log's butt flares over four kinked roots that run out low and down into the shingle on one side, with no fork, no knob and nothing curving back. The shore is a broad open beach of rounded shingle with a dark drift line of fine debris, running out of both edges of the frame; there is NO WATER in the file, because water drawn behind a pile of wood is a dam and a channel with a far bank is a stream - the river is the level's parallax behind this prop. No bark, no green wood, no saw cut, no tool mark, no point, no disc or ring. Natural debris and nothing else: no cairn, no inuksuk, no marker, no structure, no shelter, no fish weir and no figure at any scale - assets/style/the-north-level.md and docs/content-review.md. Drawn from the driftwood along the shore in assets/refs/the-north/yukon-river-bluff-and-aspen.jpg and the log jam on the bar in yukon-river-valley.jpg; see assets/refs/references.json, subject driftwood-pile. Generated from a centreline-and-thickness description of each log, so its numbers are coordinates rather than hand-placed points. POI hero, present at every visual tier.
